adversarialReview.what: The card's Williamson fixture is a JOIN MISS. Live Williamson is a JOIN HIT on the R-prefix CAD slice. Gap ledger section 7: identity join rate 1.0 on 282,570 landing keys; dollars/living live on 319,480 numeric keys. R6B's negative control ('Williamson improvement stays unaccounted — if it moved, STOP, the scoping leaked') is therefore unsatisfiable under identity join plus a matched-row emission.
adversarialReview.mechanism1: Card authors treated 'values exist under a different key' as a join miss. Rejected as the live mechanism: the fill already matches every R-prefix landing key to an R-prefix CAD row (apn/acres/legal/market/situs stamped).
adversarialReview.mechanism2Accepted: Identity join hits the R-prefix row; improvement is null ON THAT ROW. A matched-row emission will convert those cells to absent-verified. That is field-level authority (the numeric row is the value-bearing account) leaking into a row-level rule. Not a join-miss leak.
adversarialReview.disposition: Implement the structural row-level rule the dispatch asked for. Do not add an R-prefix or 48491 runtime skip (that is the bypassable check the card forbids). Name the live match-hit as the contradiction. R6B must not treat a moved Williamson improvement cell as proof the join-miss scope leaked — it proves the card's fixture and the live store are different shapes.
adversarialReview.livingZeroVsNull: Collapsed 0-and-null would convert living 0 to absent-verified. Forbidden. Separate branches.
adversarialReview.dollarZeroVsNull: Collapsed would convert $0 to absent-verified. Forbidden.
adversarialReview.stampGuardVsR1: kind !== unaccounted means a later crosswalked VALUE cannot overwrite absent-verified. If R6B identity-joins Williamson before R1, those cells lock. R1B leave_behind.
adversarialReview.applyCadScalarExport: Will not export. A public emitCadNullVerified would let a join-miss caller fire the emission.
